hooks.text: The most famous star in the sky ranks 48th in brightness.
Earth's most important navigation star is surprisingly faint in the night sky.
Forty-seven stars in the night sky shine brighter than the North Star.

title: The North Star Brightness Myth Busted
description: Polaris isn't even in the top forty brightest stars in the night sky. Here is why the North Star is famous despite its dim appearance.

beats.text: The most famous star in the sky ranks 48th in brightness.
beats.visual: Long exposure photograph of circumpolar star trails around Polaris, 2021

beats.text: Millions of skywatchers mistakenly believe Polaris is the brightest star above Earth.
beats.visual: Wide field telescope photograph of constellation Ursa Minor and Polaris, 2020

beats.text: In reality, Sirius blazes roughly 25 times brighter because it sits only 8.7 light-years away.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope photograph of binary star system Sirius A and B, 2005
queries: Sirius A and B Hubble Space Telescope

beats.text: Polaris sits over 430 light-years away, though it is intrinsically thousands of times more luminous than our Sun.
beats.visual: NASA artist concept of yellow supergiant star Polaris Aa, 2006
queries: Yellow supergiant star artist concept NASA

beats.text: Navigators rely on Polaris solely because it aligns almost directly above Earth's northern rotational axis.
beats.visual: Astronomical diagram showing how Big Dipper pointer stars lead to Polaris, 2018
queries: Big Dipper pointer stars Polaris diagram
Ursa Major pointer stars Polaris guide

beats.text: But Earth wobbles on its rotational axis over a 26,000-year cycle called precession.
beats.visual: Diagram illustrating Earth's axial precession wobble over 26,000 years, 2019

beats.text: Around the year 2100, Polaris reaches its closest northern alignment before slowly drifting away.
beats.visual: Celestial map showing path of north celestial pole through constellations, 2022
queries: North celestial pole precession path diagram

beats.text: In 13,000 years, the brilliant star Vega will take over as our new North Star.
beats.visual: Telescope photograph of bright star Vega in constellation Lyra, 2021

beats.text: Until then, many will still falsely assume that the North Star is the brightest.
beats.visual: Wide night sky photo showing the Big Dipper pointing to Polaris, 2023
queries: Big Dipper pointer stars Polaris night sky photo
